cases.H05: Exactly one requested native exec_command; old hook's denial is a retained regression FAIL. Updated hook must allow and print BOUND_WRITE_ACCEPTED; no retries/bypass. Static classification only; no claim of end-to-end file copying.
cases.H06: Exactly one requested native exec_command; real one-file hook must deny two read expressions even alongside a bound write destination. SHOULD_NOT_RUN must not be process stdout. No retries/bypass.
cases.H07: Two bounded head -c 64 commands, both labelled and dispatched in one executor wave; no other file/path/schema reads. Final reports explore and tea-rags-core. Count model response waves, not native child tool calls.
cases.S01: Strict baseline and candidate must deny the one command reading two Markdown files. Experimental bounded-head policy alone may allow it; require actual head output with both labelled file headers and name fields. No retry/splitting. Compare successful experimental model waves with H07 parallel per-file reads, not with a denied strict read as a claimed speedup.
cases.S02: All policies must deny two head -c 5000 reads: combined data exceeds the experimental 8192-byte cap even before headers. No process stdout or retry/bypass.

adoption: Production retains one Markdown input per command. The bounded-head prototype is unshipped, direct-command-only, with at most two literal paths and a proved combined byte bound including head headers. No file-size guessing. Acceptance/safety does not establish a speed benefit. Do not ship it without a demonstrated useful model-step/context result and retained controls.
